$comment: W-4 (I-3) — reviewed exception register for the service-client principal check.
Three lists, three different meanings. Do not merge them.
exceptions — a route with a VERIFIED orthogonal authorization model. Reviewed and permanent.
Adding one is a security decision: name the model and cite the line that enforces it.
baseline   — a route with NO verified model. Real W-15 remediation work, frozen 2026-07-31.
FROZEN: entries may be removed as they are fixed, never added.
advisory_transitive_only — reaches a service client through a helper rather than importing one,
so it is outside the enforced predicate. Listed so the set cannot grow silently.
All three lists may only shrink. A stale entry fails the check.
The `ratchet` ceilings below are ENFORCED BY THE CHECK, not only by the lock. Over the
ceiling is a violation; under it is stale, because a ceiling left above a fallen floor hands
out that many free exceptions. Both must be re-tightened whenever the floor moves.

history: 2026-08-04: unresolved re-tightened 26 → 17 after the book-v2 retirement; advisory left at 3.
2026-08-06: unresolved re-tightened 17 → 15; advisory raised 3 → 10 and moved under enforcement.
The 3 → 10 raise is not a shrink. It ratifies a growth that already happened in e7e585010 and
9187ae81a and was never bounded: 5 genuinely new public tour routes, plus `resolve` and `slots`
which moved OFF `exceptions` when the service client migrated into `guardTourActionRoute`.

Advisory raised 10 → 12: `book` completed the same guard migration as sibling tour routes, and
`confirm-attendance` is a new public tour route on the same capability-token model.

exceptions.reason: Read-only action-link metadata. The row is selected BY the bearer token (`.eq("token", token)` at :22) — the token is the authorization, per I-4. No caller-supplied row selector.
Row selected by the bearer token (:17). Expiry and single-use are checked and return 410 (verified by phase 3 §13.1 / I-4).
Row selected by the bearer token from the query string (:20). Same action_links capability as /action/[token].
Row selected by the bearer token from the body (:75), documented as the same raw action_links.token as the /action/[token] URL.
Row selected by the bearer token (:37); validity, consumption and expiry are checked before the write.
Embed bootstrap. `resolvePublicFormEmbedContext(supabase, token)` (:31) is the gate; every subsequent read is scoped to what the token resolved.
Creates a draft tied to the resolved public link (:46). Creates only — no caller-supplied row selector.

Takes a caller-supplied submissionId, but binds it: `verifySubmissionBelongsToPublicEmbed(supabase, ctx, submissionId)` at :58 (GET) and :144 (PATCH) runs before the read/update. This is the subject-bound property I-4 requires.
Same binding check at :114 before the submit path executes.

Svix `Webhook.verify` against RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET at :69, and it returns 400 before `createAdminClient()` is constructed at :91 — no statement reaches the database on an unsigned request. The handler documents that session auth MUST NOT gate it.

GET returning (id, name, slug) for active rows of the platform-global `verticals` table. No org-scoped or personal data, no caller-supplied selector, no write. RLS bypass discloses nothing tenant-specific.
Pricing/addon catalogs for the public booking UI. The org is pinned to ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID from the environment (:26) — never caller-supplied — and the handler is read-only.
Org pinned to ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID and 500s without it (:17-20); entity_type is validated against a fixed allow-list (:32-38). Read-only, returns only fields explicitly flagged for public booking.
Unauthenticated vendor application intake. Org pinned to ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID and 500s without it (:33-37). Creates only — it selects no existing row by a caller-supplied id.

advisory_transitive_only.reason: Public inbound gutter-lead intake. Reaches a service client through `@/lib/supabase` helpers rather than importing a constructor, so it sits outside the enforced predicate. Creates only (contact upsert + opportunity create); marked LEGACY_COMPAT in its own header. Flagged for W-15.

Twilio status callback; delegates to `handleTwilioSmsStatus`, which holds the service client. Webhook model — signature verification lives in the helper, not the route, which is why the route itself shows no principal.
Per-tenant subaccount variant of the same handler and the same model.

Recipient-scoped capability token, not a session principal. The route no longer constructs a service client: `guardTourActionRoute` (:39) holds it and returns it only after `authorizeTourAction` verifies the token hash, the link↔invitation recipient binding, and the action kind. `requiredActions` is the route constant `REQUIRED_ACTIONS` (:27-35) — never request-supplied. CORRECTED 2026-08-06: that constant now lists all seven action kinds, so the previous reason's claim that `[view_tour_slots, view_tour_details]` keeps a decline- or cancel-only token from reading context is NO LONGER TRUE. The widening is deliberate and argued in the route header (:18-25) — any credential on the same invitation may re-read what the invitation already disclosed to that same recipient — and the authorizer still proves recipient binding, expiry and revocation. Read-only; discloses labels and status, never a person, opportunity, process or household id.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[view_tour_slots, reschedule_tour, select_tour_slot]` (:26) — CORRECTED 2026-08-06: `select_tour_slot` was added to the constant and the previous reason still named only the first two. The authorized link scopes the availability read, and the guard rate-limits per token under the `slots` budget.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[decline_tour]` (:14). Single-use: `consumeTourAction` closes the credential with a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL`. Writes only the invitation's own decline state.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[confirm_tour]` (:19). The booking id comes from the credential via `loadBoundBooking`, never from the request body, so no caller-supplied selector reaches the write.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[reschedule_tour]` (:24). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`; the requested slot is revalidated against `computeAvailableTourSlots` before `rescheduleTourBooking` runs.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[cancel_tour]` (:16). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`, and the cancel is single-use through `consumeTourAction`.

Recipient-scoped capability token, not a session principal. Same guard-held client and model as the other public tour routes: `guardTourActionRoute` holds the service client and returns it only after `authorizeTourAction` verifies the token hash, the link↔invitation recipient binding, and the action kind. Route constant `[view_tour_details]` (:26) — a read-only Manage credential, so the caller cannot mutate. It mints a single-use `cancel_tour` credential bound to the booking loaded from the credential via `loadBoundBooking`, never from the request; it performs no cancellation itself.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[select_tour_slot, view_tour_slots]` (:36). Commitment consumes the select action (or finds the sibling select link when the reusable view credential is presented); booking write is invitation-bound, never a caller-supplied booking id. Rate-limited inside `guardTourActionRoute` under the `book` budget.

Same guard-held client and same capability model. Route constant `[confirm_attendance]` (:14). Booking id is credential-bound via `loadBoundBooking`; attendance affirmation does not change booking status_key and is idempotent through `confirmTourAttendance`.

reviewed_note: 2026-08-03: dropped stale book-v2 entries after routes were removed from the tree (lists may only shrink). 2026-08-04 re-review: all 17 remaining entries re-checked against the tree — every one still exists, still holds a service client, and still resolves no principal (asserted by the lock). Citations spot-verified line-by-line for the two subject-binding entries (:58/:144, :114) and the tour-booking token resolve (:30). The ratchet ceiling was tightened 26 → 17 to match the post-retirement floor. 2026-08-06 reopen re-execution: the lock was RED on this base — the advisory ratchet capped the set at 3 while 10 routes qualified. Root cause: the ceilings lived only in the lock, so an allow-list-only commit could grow a list with `prebuild` still green. The ceilings now sit in this file and the check enforces them, over AND under. All 15 exceptions re-checked; unresolved re-tightened 17 → 15. Every advisory `requiredActions` citation was re-verified against the tree and four were wrong: three drifted line numbers (`slots` :20→:26, `reschedule` :21→:24, `resolve` :16→:27-35) and one substantive — `resolve`'s reason claimed a two-action constant that now lists all seven kinds, so the property it asserted was false. Corrected in place rather than silently rewritten. 2026-08-14: staging prebuild RED after PR #416 — `book` no longer directly imports a service client (stale exception) while both `book` and new `confirm-attendance` are transitive-only via `guardTourActionRoute`. Moved `book` off exceptions onto advisory; listed `confirm-attendance`; re-tightened unresolved 15 → 14; raised advisory ceiling 10 → 12 with history.
